newsitem.title: UK: Lloyds TSB shuffles board, makes insurance buy.
newsitem.headline: Lloyds TSB shuffles board, makes insurance buy.

text.p: Lloyds TSB Group, Britain's largest retail financial services company, on Friday ended months of speculation over the future of its chief executive Brian Pitman by making him chairman and elevating his deputy.

The company named former TSB chief executive Peter Ellwood to the top job in a move likely to be greeted with relief by city analysts who had hoped for an internal appointment which would help continue the bank's recent good results record.

Lloyds TSB followed the news of its board changes by also ending speculation over its 62.6 percent-owned Lloyds Abbey Life insurance unit which is seperately quoted on the stock exchange. It said it will pay 635p per share to buy-out the minority shareholding in the company in a shares and cash deal amounting to some 1.66 billion pounds.
The deal ended months of market talk as to the future of Lloyds Abbey which had included its possible sale to Prudential Corp.
Lloyds TSB said the proposal was in the best interests of customers, staff and shareholders.
Lloyds Abbey shares were 35p higher at 627p while Lloyds TSB dipped 9p to 382.
Lloyds said its current chairman Robin Ibbs will retire in February.
